run.question:
Look at the elasticsearch index 'app-278-events-n8c3v6q1': list which
fields it has (with their types), and using the index's actual field
names tell me how many documents in it are ERROR level.

report.summary: The index 'app-278-events-n8c3v6q1' exists (health green, open, docs.count 27, store.size 7.1kb) and maps exactly four top-level fields: app (keyword), lvl (keyword), ts (date) and txt (text). There is no field named 'level'; the log-level field in this index is named lvl, and ts (not @timestamp) is the mapped date field used for the time filter. Over the authorized window (2026-10-24T18:14:49Z to 2026-11-23T18:14:49Z on field ts), the index matches 27 documents (total relation eq), and a terms aggregation on lvl splits them into INFO 12, ERROR 9, WARN 6 with sum_other_doc_count 0. An independent filtered count with the exact-term query {"term": {"lvl": "ERROR"}} also returns 9, so 9 documents in this index are ERROR level under its actual field name lvl. Sampled document timestamps in the returned views were around 2026-11-23T18:11-18:13Z. This was a data-inspection question, not an incident, so no root cause is named.

claims.text: Index 'app-278-events-n8c3v6q1' maps four top-level fields with their types: app=keyword, lvl=keyword, ts=date, txt=text.
Index 'app-278-events-n8c3v6q1' is open with health green, docs.count 27 and store.size 7.1kb at query time.

Over the authorized window on time field ts, the index matches 27 documents, and a terms aggregation on field lvl yields buckets INFO 12, ERROR 9, WARN 6 (sum_other_doc_count 0, doc_count_error_upper_bound 0, 1 successful shard and 0 failed).
A filtered count with {"term": {"lvl": "ERROR"}} on the same index and window returns 9 documents (total relation eq), confirming 9 ERROR-level documents under the index's actual field name lvl.

gaps: The ERROR count of 9 is scoped to the authorized window applied to field ts; documents whose ts falls outside that window are not reflected in these counts, and the time field is the writer's timestamp, not necessarily event time.

Two earlier search attempts were rejected with TIME_FIELD_REQUIRED because the index does not map @timestamp but maps ts; those attempts returned no data and were re-run successfully with time_field=ts. Nothing is claimed from the rejected attempts.
Because lvl is mapped as keyword and the exact term 'ERROR' was used, case variants such as 'error' or 'Error' would not be counted; no such variants appeared among the returned lvl buckets.
The mapping describes declared properties only; whether every document actually carries all four fields, and any documents' full _source content, was not verified.
The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so no index change history could be checked (not required for this question).
next_steps: If a case-insensitive or broader level inventory is needed, re-run the lvl aggregation over a narrower window or with a normalized keyword field.
If document contents matter, sample documents with a _source filter on ['ts','app','lvl','txt'] to inspect actual log lines.
